entry.title: programming • Re: Writing games for the Tube
entry.content:
According to Mark Moxon's article on second proccessor Elite, the Tube software on the host processor uses the language zero page up to 0x7F. Hence, 0x80 to 0x8F is free for your USERV handler or similar application routines on the host processor. I don't know off hand if there's any more official source for this information, but it makes sense that some zero page is reserved for application use on the host.

My own work-in-progress game, Japanese Military Chess, dynamically supports running on the host or 6502 second processor. I've been keeping a dev log and you can read the section on how I implemented Tube support here: https://www.robinkay.uk/posts/2024/01/04/jmc-part-2/

entry.title: 8-bit acorn software: other • Acorn File Forge: a browser-based editor for SSD, MMB, ADFS, BeebSCSI, HFE and UEF images
entry.content:
Hi all,

I have been working on a utility called Acorn File Forge. It started with a fairly simple idea: open an MMB file and an ADFS hard-drive image side by side, then drag software between them without juggling several command-line tools (as cool as they are, and as much as I love the command line, I'm also a visual person ).

As these things tend to do, it grew a little.

Acorn File Forge runs in a web browser and supports up to three rearrangeable work panes. Each pane can contain a different image, so you can browse an MMB in one, open one of its disks in another, and copy files or complete disks into an ADFS hard drive in the third.

It currently supports:
  • SSD and DSD DFS images
  • MMB disk collections, including all 511 slots
  • ADFS floppy images
  • BeebSCSI DAT and DSC hard-drive pairs
  • HDF, HDD and raw FileCore images
  • HFE floppy images
  • UEF tapes
  • ZIP archives containing supported images
Files and directories can be added, extracted, renamed, moved, deleted, locked and dragged between compatible images. ADFS directories are fully traversable, and multiple files or MMB slots can be selected at once.

MMB and menu support

MMB support includes blank SSD and DSD creation, read-only and read/write slot flags, moving disks by drag and drop, multi-image imports, duplicate-game checks and menu maintenance.

It understands the Universal Menu, SPI Game Menu, Electron User and Acorn User menu arrangements. Menu databases can be previewed, bulk edited, reordered, audited and regenerated.

There is similar menu support for ADFS directories. A collection of extracted disks can be turned into a browsable menu, with Acorn File Forge examining the actual launchers to determine whether each title needs CHAIN, RUN, EXEC or LOAD. It also derives PAGE from the program wherever possible instead of relying on a hopeful guess.

Online software library

The Online Library can search several configurable Acorn software catalogues. Results can be filtered by machine and installed directly into an MMB, DFS disk or ADFS directory.

It tries to use filenames, existing menu records, disk catalogues and loaders before going online for metadata.

Safety and recovery

Because old disk images can be wonderfully inventive, the application takes a cautious approach.

It works on private copies, creates automatic undo points, supports named checkpoints and validates images before saving. Long operations have progress displays and abort controls.

Saved images arrive as timestamped ZIP files with a generated README containing checksums, hardware information, warnings and a catalogue of the contents.

There are hardware profiles for:
  • Electron Plus 3
  • BBC Micro with MMFS
  • BBC/Master BeebSCSI
  • Master ADFS
  • Archimedes and RISC OS
These help catch things such as unsuitable PAGE values, Tube-related Electron problems and invalid BeebSCSI geometry.

Running it

It is fully Dockerised and listens on port 8666:

Code: 

git clone git@github.com:peteclarke-del/AcornFileForge.git
cd AcornFileForge
docker compose up --build -d
Then visit:

Code: 

http://localhost:8666
The source and full illustrated guide are here:

Acorn File Forge on GitHub

This is very much aimed at real Acorn workflows, but unusual loaders, protected disks and obscure FileCore variants will always find creative ways to surprise software. Please keep original images and test anything important before writing it back to physical media.

I would be particularly interested in feedback from people using MMFS, BeebSCSI, Electron Plus 3 and real Archimedes or RISC OS hardware. Bug reports, awkward images and suggestions for less confusing workflows are all welcome.

Hopefully somebody else finds it useful, or at least enjoys seeing just how far “I only want to copy this disk into that image” can escalate.

entry.title: programming • Re: Writing games for the Tube: bare metal
entry.content:
Using a faster parasite CPU does not make the Tube any faster. The bottleneck is the host's ability to read and write data via the ULA between the CPUs.
This is strictly true but having a very fast parasite (i.e. native mode Pi) does mean that you can get away without checking that data has arrived on the host side during longer transfers. This is a significant performance improvement.
